seoTitle: How to Create a New Outlook Account for Free
metaDescription: Create a free Outlook.com account: pick a username, set a password that meets Microsoft's requirements, get through the verification step, and set up a passkey or recovery option.
intro: Setting up a free Outlook.com inbox is a short flow, but it branches depending on where you land first, and skipping the recovery step at the end leaves the account with no way back in if you're ever locked out. This guide follows the sign-up from outlook.com through username selection, password, and the profile and verification screens. It's aimed at someone creating a fresh personal inbox, not migrating an existing Microsoft 365 account.

steps.heading: Start from the Outlook landing page
steps.body: Go to outlook.com and you land on a page with two options: Sign in for an existing account, or Create a free account for a new one. The button repeats in the hero section and again in the footer, so it's hard to miss no matter how far you scroll. This is also the page a plain outlook.com link from a friend or coworker lands you on, so recognize it as the right starting point instead of hunting for a separate sign-up page.

image.caption: The Outlook.com welcome page, with Sign in and Create a free account buttons in the header and hero section.

steps.heading: Use the sign-in screen's link if you land there instead
steps.body: Some links point straight to the plain Microsoft sign-in box, asking for an email, phone number, or Skype name, instead of the outlook.com landing page. That's not a dead end. Below the input field sits a "No account? Create one!" link that opens the same registration flow.

image.caption: The Microsoft sign-in screen, with a "No account? Create one!" link beneath the email field for starting a new registration.

steps.heading: Choose your username and domain
steps.body: Registration starts with a Create your Microsoft account screen asking for a new email address. Type the handle you want on the left, and confirm the domain with the dropdown on the right; @outlook.com is the default, and Microsoft sometimes offers @hotmail.com in the same menu. You won't find out whether the handle is taken until after you click Next, so have a couple of backup variations ready.

image.caption: The Create your Microsoft account screen, with a new email handle being typed in and the @outlook.com domain selected from the dropdown.

steps.heading: Create a password
steps.body: The next screen pairs a password with the address. Mix uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and a symbol, and don't reuse a password from another account that matters to you. A visibility toggle on the field lets you check what you typed before continuing. A typo here means troubleshooting a lockout before the account even exists.

steps.heading: Provide your profile details
steps.body: Microsoft then asks for your first name, last name, region or country, and date of birth. These aren't filler fields. Your date of birth determines certain account protections, and in some regions signing up under the local minimum age requires a parent or guardian to complete the process instead of you. Enter real values, since correcting them later is more involved than getting them right the first time.

steps.heading: Verify you're human, then set up a way back in
steps.body: Before the account activates, you'll typically solve a short puzzle confirming a person is signing up, not a script. After that, Microsoft offers to add a passkey using your device's fingerprint or PIN, or a backup phone number or alternate email for recovery instead. Set up at least one of the two in the same session. Skipping both leaves no way to recover the account if you're ever locked out. Microsoft then finishes building the mailbox, and the new inbox loads on its own.

faq.question: Is creating an Outlook account free?
faq.answer: Yes. Sign-up gives you a free Outlook.com inbox with 15 GB of dedicated mail storage, plus 5 GB of OneDrive storage shared across OneDrive, Outlook attachments, and the free Microsoft 365 web apps.

faq.question: What if my desired username is already taken?
faq.answer: You'll only find out after clicking Next on the email address screen, since usernames are unique across the whole @outlook.com domain. Have a variation ready.

faq.question: Do I need to add a backup phone number?
faq.answer: It's optional, but it's offered in the same step as the passkey option for a reason: skipping both leaves the account with no recovery path if you lose access.

faq.question: Does Microsoft require a parent's involvement for a younger user?
faq.answer: In regions where the signup age falls below the local minimum, yes. Microsoft asks a parent or guardian to complete part of the process instead of the account holder.

faq.question: Can I go straight to account creation without the sign-in screen first?
faq.answer: Yes. The outlook.com landing page has its own Create a free account button, so the sign-in screen's "Create one!" link is only needed if that's where a link happened to send you.
